messages:
maria: Heads-up — getting a steady stream of 429s for tenant `acme` on dedicated pool `eu-west-1-ded-3`. Started ~2026-03-16 20:12 UTC. Customer reports increased latency then immediate 429s. Sample response below.

benj_oncall: Thanks — can you paste the raw error body and approximate QPS/burst numbers? Any config changes or plan upgrades recently?

maria: Sample curl + response: 
```bash
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer x...' https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limit",
  "message": "tenant rate limit exceeded",
  "retry_after": 2
}
```
QPS: steady ~70 rps, spikes to ~220 for short bursts (30-60s). They upgraded from "pro" -> "business" yesterday via billing UI.

benj_oncall: OK. Can you grab the tenant quota record from admin API and paste it? Also the translated normalized rate that the quota-manager is using (we can see mismatches there).

maria: Pulled from admin API: 
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "acme",
  "configured_unit": "minute",
  "configured_requests": 6000,
  "stored_normalized_rps": 1.6666667,
  "stored_as": "rps"
}
```
Note: UI shows 6000/min which the customer expects to mean 100 rps. But stored_normalized_rps=1.6667 rps (i.e., ~100/hr).

kevin_infra: That stored_normalized_rps looks wrong — sounds like unit conversion bug during the plan migration. If 6000/min should be 100/s, getting 1.6667 implies someone converted minute -> hour (6000/3600=1.6667). So the translator probably used seconds_per_unit=3600 instead of 60.

alex_sre: Corroborating: I checked the quota-migration job logs around the time of the plan upgrade. There's a migration task that maps "minute" -> seconds multiplier; I see a regression where the enum mapping for "minute" accidentally maps to HOURS in the new codepath. Log snippet: 
```
2026-03-16T19:58:03Z migration: tenant acme plan migrate v2
migration: unit_map.get('minute') -> 3600
applied_rate = configured_requests / 3600 -> 1.6667 rps
```

maria: That explains why even moderate load trips 429s. But I also see autoscaler events around same timeframe: pool had CPU jump and only scaled after ~5m. Might be a compounding issue.

kevin_infra: Looking at autoscaler metrics: target_replicas should have gone from 2 -> 4 at 20:11:40, but cooldown window is 300s and last scale was 20:07:30, so autoscaler refused immediate additional scaling until cooldown expired. New replica added at 20:16:00 (too late).

benj_oncall: So root cause appears to be two things coinciding: 1) quota migration bug that mis-translated "per-minute" to per-hour, drastically lowering effective rps; 2) autoscaler cooldown/policies delayed scale-up so dedicated pool couldn't absorb the burst.\n
alex_sre: Immediate mitigations: 
- Admin override to bump normalized_rps for acme to 500 rps temporarily. API: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.test/v1/tenants/acme/overrides \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer admin...' \\n  -d '{"temp_rps":500, "expires_in":600}'
```
- Reduce autoscaler cooldown for pool `eu-west-1-ded-3` from 300s -> 60s (manual adjustment) to allow faster scale for next bursts.

kevin_infra: I'm applying both. Pushed override at 20:20:05 and lowered cooldown at 20:21:10. Will monitor.

maria: Customer on call — they saw error rate drop after 20:21. I'll message them and keep them updated.

benj_oncall: Post-mortem action items: 
- Fix migration unit-map regression (minute -> 60s). Add unit mapping tests.
- Add detection alert if stored_normalized_rps deviates >10% from expected configured_requests/units for any tenant during migration.
- Consider temporary safe-guard: do not apply migrations that would decrease normalized_rps by >50% without manual confirmation.

alex_sre: I'll open a PR and include a regression test plus a small migration rollback script to correct affected tenants. Quick scan shows ~8 tenants touched by the same migration job in last 24h.

maria: Thanks everyone. Customer follow-up message I sent: "We've applied a temporary rate override and sped up scaling; root cause was a config migration bug + autoscaler cooldown overlap. We'll revert override once fixed and confirm new quota values. Apologies — working on permanent fix." :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2045 - "Tenant quota migration unit mapping bug causing unexpected throttles" assigned to eng-ml and eng-platform.

benj_oncall: Great. Keep this thread updated with the PR and rollback status.

maria: Will update once rollback script runs and we verify normalized_rps values for acme and the other affected tenants.

alex_sre: PR link: https://git.redwood/eng/infra/merge_requests/987 (fix + tests). Rolling migration script scheduled: 2026-03-17 02:00 UTC.

kevin_infra: Confirmed post-rollback normalized_rps for acme = 100.0 rps at 2026-03-17T02:05:10Z. Marking incident as mitigated pending customer sign-off.

maria: Customer confirmed restored service quality. Closing loop.

benj_oncall: Nice work. Add a KB note for support on "quota migration mismatches" and steps for temporary overrides.
